near_duplicate_groups.decision: Exact duplicate: retain/recover 027 only; 313 contributes provenance, not a second accepted row.

Retain both: command substitution invokes one removal even on empty expansion (then missing-argument failure) and can hit argument-size limits; GNU xargs -r invokes none on empty input and batches nonempty input to argument limits. Both remain destructive ask for nonempty volume lists. This is composition/empty-input semantics, not flag-spelling diversity.

Retain: rm status=exited is an explicit status selection; container prune excludes pod-associated stopped containers and 024 additionally restricts creation age. Do not assume identical selected sets.
Retain dependency recursion, forced all-container scope, image ancestry, mounted-volume selection, and network membership: substantive selection mechanisms, not resource-name substitutions.
Retain forced all pods versus stopped-pod prune with confirmation. Local Podman pods are not Kubernetes API objects.
Retain all-volume rm without forced dependent removal, forced named-volume removal with dependent containers, versus unused-volume prune; no force-only alias duplicate.
Retain default service/network teardown versus orphan expansion versus service-image removal. None is allow merely because -v is absent.
Retain broad Docker container inventory versus retained pre_start-hook label subset; 316 is independently safe related partial inspection, not a duplicate formatting variant.

candidate_evidence.finding: Exact rm --all example; removes all Buildah working containers, unmounting when needed. Separate containers manual establishes metadata listing of working containers and base images; 302 is safe relevant inventory.

Literal prune --force example. --force is documented to remove all containers using an image before removing that image; not merely a no-confirmation flag. Description appropriately includes cache/intermediate images and possible dependent-container removal. 302 is preliminary inspection, not complete cache-prune simulation.

All six literal examples are present. --depend recursively removes dependents; without force running/unusable containers are refused. -f -a includes running/paused, and force may remove container-storage entries from other engines. status=exited is not exit-code filtering; ancestor includes descendants; volume/network select associated containers but do not themselves request deleting those volume/network objects. Existing 015 is safe related enumeration.

Exact all-force example; force stops running containers, removes containers then pods. Local runtime grouping, CAT-3.3 rather than Kubernetes deletion. 015 shows component containers, not pod topology or exact removal plan.

Literal examples confirmed. --all without force cannot remove in-use volumes; --force myvol removes using containers first and may stop running containers. 022 is independent safe inventory of the same volume domain.

Exact sudo podman pod prune example and displayed confirmation remove stopped/exited pods and their containers. Ask/high is independent of displayed prompt. Force variant is withheld as 325, not silently interpreted.

All three literal commands occur in tldr with no invented option combinations. Current Compose reference confirms external networks/volumes are excluded; anonymous volumes retained by default are not automatically remounted on subsequent up. All variants remove containers and can cause downtime and writable-state loss; --rmi all adds service-image deletion and --remove-orphans adds services not in current file. Default down also removes retained failed pre_start-hook containers.

Literal metadata listing recommended by official down documentation before teardown. Filters all containers by pre_start-hook label, without running hooks or Compose lifecycle actions. Related partial preflight is defensible as a safe alternative to proceeding immediately with deletion, not a claim to list all affected service containers, networks, images, volumes or only the current project.

Both literal shell compositions occur under Docker >=1.9 notes. Only CLI invocations extracted; historical helper script never executed or proposed as safe. dangling=true means no container references, not data expendability; older README claims about prune internals are not imported. GNU xargs reference confirms -r skips invocation when input has no nonblanks and xargs batches at size limits.

Both literal examples occur in Node-Level Operations. Source caption incorrectly calls --all --force stopped-only. Static official removeContainerCommand flag/help and flow explicitly select all, stop RUNNING with timeout 0 under force, call RemoveContainer and attempt log/rotation cleanup unless keep-logs. Description does not imply guaranteed cleanup success. Runtime host container deletion is CAT-3.3 even when the runtime backs Kubernetes; it is not Kubernetes API bulk resource deletion. ps -a is independently read-only listing.

Literal commands in MIT README Everyday Commands. README describes Incus system containers and persistent environments; development/agent isolation is not evidence their state is disposable. Official Container-Operations wiki corroborates plain clean stops at stopped containers; sessions/orphans/pools need their own flags or --all, despite shorthand README caption. list --all includes active containers and saved sessions, without removal.

Literal inline nerdctl system prune appears in BuildKit dependency note, not executed trace. Pinned command-reference calls it unused-data removal, separate --all widens images, --force skips confirmation and --volumes enables volume pruning; plain form does not include volumes. Reference container-prune section specifies stopped containers. README warns older BuildKit cannot support some cache-prune features; do not infer minimum nerdctl release or successful complete cleanup.

Source lists nerdctl ps {{[-a|--all]}} and describes running and stopped containers. Selecting the explicit -a alternative and removing tldr markup is documented extraction, not model-built semantics. Listing is current namespace inventory, not global containerd purge plan.

independent_label_decision.ask: Each accepted destructive operation can destroy container writable state, volumes, or related runtime resources. Visible stopped/unused/dependency/filter selectors do not establish expendability, permission, recovery or ownership; a responsible human must decide whether deletion and possible downtime are intended. Thus ask is independently supported, not a mechanical translation of source default modify. An internal prompt is not external approval. No unsupported production or backup premise is used.
independent_label_decision.severity: high is justified for multi-object state loss or a volume deletion capable of removing its dependent containers; not automatically critical absent broader evidence. Listings are low.
independent_label_decision.allow: 302/316/320/322/324 list metadata without container execution, mutation, file redirection, or content dumps. The command represented in a metadata field is not executed. Safe status is established independently of the destructive pair; listings do not reclaim space or authorize deletion.
